input.rationale: This is a hosting agreement under which HDI operates the Site, holds Company Content and user information (Section 8.1) and generates order/export files (Section 1.5). Section 4 addresses only term, notice and the Termination Payment; Sections 8 and 10.7 impose confidentiality and survival but nowhere require HDI to return or delete the Company's data or to assist with migration after the Termination Date. No transition, exit or data-return language appears anywhere in the document, so the rule's preferred position is absent and we insert a new Section 4.3 covering up to six months of transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, machine-readable data return within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter.

proposal.summary: Insert Section 4.3 requiring HDI to provide transition assistance, return Company data in machine-readable format within 30 days, and certify deletion.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 4 sets out termination mechanics and the Termination Payment but says nothing about winding down the hosted Site, so we have added an exit clause requiring HDI to return the Company's Content, user, customer and order data in a machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, provide up to six (6) months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, and certify deletion thereafter. If six months is too long, we can accept ninety (90) days of assistance with the same thirty-day data export.

ops.text: 4.3 Transition Assistance; Return of Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months following the Termination Date at HDI's then-current rates, including reasonable cooperation in migrating the Site and its operations to the Company or its designee; (b) within thirty (30) days after the Termination Date, return to the Company all Content, user information, customer data, order data and other Confidential Information of the Company then in HDI's possession or control, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all such data from its systems and certify such deletion to the Company in writing.
